newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North sees better Q4 reflected in yr.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North sees better Q4 reflected in yr.

text.p: Diversified mining house North Ltd said on Thursday an improvement in fourth quarter production and sales would be reflected in its net profit for 1996/97.
North also said the markets for some commodities would have a limiting effect on the extent of any improvement the company's financial results in 1997/98.

In its fourth quarter production report, North reported record annual production at its Robe River iron ore plant of 28.5 million tonnes, following a 16 percent improvement in the fourth quarter over the same period last year.
Annual uranium production was up 23 percent and annual zinc concentrate production reached a record level, as did fourth quarter gold production at Kanowna Belle, North said.

"The continued improvement in production and sales in the fourth quarter, from a number of the group's business units, will be reflected in our bottom line for 1996/1997," said North managing director Campbell Anderson.

Anderson said he was particularly pleased with the continued progress at the Zinkgruvan zinc mine in Sweden and the Northparkes copper and gold mine, as well as the integration of the Iron Ore Co of Canada (IOC) following North's purchase of a 59.3 percent stake for A$200 milllion in January.

"Although 1997/98 will have the benefit of the Alumbrera project coming into production later in 1997, we expect markets for some commodities to have a limiting effect on the extent of any improvement in our financial result for 1997/98," Anderson added.
Markets for iron ore and wood fibre, for example, were expected to be flat, while the uranium spot price had opened this financial year well down on last year.
Uranium prices traded between US$13-18 a pound last year, but spot prices had opened at US$10.50 a pound this year, Anderson said.
"Something in excess of 40 percent of current contracts are priced with reference to the sport market," he said.
"The group is also watching closely the mvoes and effects of the commodity prices, particularly gold, copper and zinc which were volatile in 1996/97."
North holds 68.4 percent of Energy Resources of Australia (ERA), which operates the Ranger uranium mine in the Northern Territory.
The group has 25 percent of the Bajo de Alumbrera copper and gold mine in Argentina is expected to begin production of concentrate in the current quarter.
